summary: Round 13 (clean worktree at 6d288fe, which includes 4f992d5). From the aisle the room is unchanged and still clearly the same product: q06 against c_27312, q10 against c_27315. The ash now has warm figure with long horizontal streaks where w12 had a flat linen hatch (q06 median (189,184,175), was (181,178,172)). The comforter is the main gain. It is now matte royal blue with the check jacquard and visible soft quilt boxes. The r9 diagonal ripple cluster and the pie-crust hems are gone. Studio duvet/white-pillow ratios are r9 (0.47, 0.52, 0.89) against tpg_81 white-balanced (0.46, 0.54, 1.06), close to a match. The pillow flange has gone from near white (0.89 of the white pillow) to grey (0.69; kn_17 0.45). What still holds the area below 8.5: (1) The O comforter plan is a T or cross. The wide aisle part covers only ~0.2 m beside the seat before it tapers (a = smooth(-0.80, -0.52) starts 7 cm past z0 = -0.875), so a white wedge of pad shows at the aisle between the pillows and the table corner. In tpg_81 the comforter fills the wide part of the bed to the table corner and then tapers into the footwell. (2) The buckle is still hidden. It sits at CU (0.03, -0.20), but the belt's front end is at CU (0.267, -0.203), so the buckle lands under the navy slipper pouch (o1zoom: no buckle visible). The belt is still a single flat slab with no latch half. (3) The pillows render pastel periwinkle, ~1.2x too light against tpg_81 and much lighter than kn_17. The jacquard is a uniform 45-degree harlequin; in kn_17 and tpg_81 the squares are near-aligned with the pillow edges and run in stepped diagonal bands. (4) The ash in the studio is still pale and neutral: ash/white pillow 0.94 and R/B 1.05, against tpg_81 0.85 and R/B 1.15. Its directly lit grain is weak (luma SD 2 %). Lighting (not scored): the shells read cool blue-slate in the cabin views (q06 shell (93,99,112) against c_27312 (71,64,58)).

issues.detail: O comforter plan is a T or cross: the wide aisle part is a short triangle, and a white pad wedge shows between the pillows and the table corner
issues.problem: In the O bounds, a = smooth(-0.80, -0.52, z) starts narrowing xr from 0.30 only 7.5 cm after the head edge (z0 = -0.875), while the mattress stays 0.76 m wide to z = -0.62. Beside the seat the sheet therefore tapers diagonally at once. In plan (o2) and from above (r9, o7) it reads as a band along the wall with a short tongue reaching toward the aisle. In tpg_81 the comforter covers ~85 % of the wide part of the bed, from the pillows' lower edge to the table corner, with only a straight strip of pad at the aisle edge. It then tapers into the footwell beside the table.
issues.evidence: o2_bedO_plan: the sheet is full width only between x 380 and 440 px, against a wide-part length of 135 px. tpg_81: the comforter is full width from the pillow edge (x ~620) to the table corner (x ~1050).
issues.fix: 09c roomBed O bounds: a = smooth(-0.68, -0.57, z) (hold the full width until the mattress narrows at -0.62); xr wide 0.30 -> 0.25 so a ~3 cm strip of pad shows at the aisle edge as in tpg_81 (mr 0.285 unchanged; the roll-over then only happens where xr > mr). Optionally z0 -0.875 -> -0.90 so the head edge tucks under the blue pillow.

issues.detail: Jacquard motif is a uniform 45-degree harlequin; the photos show near-axis-aligned squares in stepped diagonal bands
issues.problem: In o5 the pale diamonds are crisp, uniform and stand on their points. kn_17 shows ~1.4 cm squares with their sides close to parallel to the pillow edges; alternating light and dark runs form stepped diagonal bands. tpg_81 shows the same cells as offset rectangles forming stair-steps. The tone-on-tone contrast in both is softer than the model's crisp pale squares.
issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py j_pillow (drawn tile): draw an axis-aligned checkerboard of 1.4 cm cells and offset every other column by half a cell (stair-step), giving diagonal banding; lower the light/dark amplitude by ~30 %. Keep the 1.9 cm period from tpg_46.
